Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • 3-day history of wheeze, cough (non-productive), shortness of breath on exertion; occasional difficulty completing sentences.  
  • Past history of childhood and adult asthma, hay fever (allergic rhinitis) and eczema.  
  • Possible viral trigger or seasonal allergen exposure discussed.

- Relevant family medical history: Not recorded.

- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  • Salbutamol inhaler – patient-reported intermittent use (“every few weeks,” “with exercise”); dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • No regular hay-fever medication.  
  • New plan: salbutamol 2–4 puffs every 4 hrs PRN (prescribed today); antihistamine OTC recommended; peak-flow meter and spacer prescribed.

- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.

- Sexual and reproductive health: Lives with partner; no other details recorded.

- Physical activity and nutrition:
  • Previously walked to work; currently unable due to breathlessness.  
  • Diet not discussed.

- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:
  • Non-smoker.  
  • Alcohol: 1 glass of wine approximately every 2–3 days.  
  • Recreational drugs: Not recorded.

- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.

- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk): Not recorded.

- Vision problems or recent changes: Not recorded.

- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:
  • Lives with partner.  
  • Occupation: Engineer (currently working from home or on sick leave).  
  • No caring responsibilities noted.

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded.
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated): Not recorded.
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums): Not recorded.
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed): Not recorded.
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen): Not recorded.
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria): Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed): Not recorded.
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due): Not recorded.
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35): Not recorded.
- Mammogram (if eligible): Not recorded.
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D): Not recorded.

Management Plan

- Prescribed peak-flow meter and spacer; pharmacist to demonstrate correct use.  
- Increase salbutamol to 2–4 puffs every 4 hours via spacer until symptoms settle.  
- Start regular OTC antihistamine for hay fever (specific product to be advised in notes).  
- Monitor peak-flow readings twice daily (morning and evening) for one week; record values.  
- Safety-netting: If fever develops, wheeze worsens, or breathlessness increases, call clinic immediately or seek urgent care.  
- Follow-up telehealth or in-person asthma review booked/planned in 1 week to assess control and consider additional controller therapy.  
- Education: spacer technique, trigger avoidance, importance of regular monitoring.

Consider:
- Future comprehensive asthma action plan and preventive inhaler at review.
- CTG registration and preventive health check (influenza vaccine, pneumococcal if indicated).

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note):

● Missing but clinically expected elements: BP, pulse, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, height/weight/BMI, waist circumference, oral/ear/vision exams, urinalysis, immunisation review, cervical screening status, mental health screening, detailed sexual health/STI screen, diet assessment, hearing assessment.  
● Internal contradictions: Patient stated asthma stopped 3–4 years ago yet also reports ongoing intermittent salbutamol use (“normally”); conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Occasional unclear or incomplete responses; overall adequate to capture main clinical details but several data points not elicited.
